title: Families, Housing, Community Services and Indigenous Affairs and Other Legislation Amendment (2008 Budget and Other Measures) Bill 2008
portfolio: Families, Community Services and Indigenous Affairs

divisions.question: That the amendments ( **Mrs Bronwyn Bishop’s** ) be agreed to.
That the amendment ( **Senator Siewert’s** ) be agreed to.

speeches.speaker: John Faulkner
speeches.brief: The bills were introduced together, with a motion to proceed without formalities and be read a first time, which was agreed to.

speeches.speaker: John Faulkner
speeches.brief: The speech introduced bills to implement the Montreal Convention for international air carrier liability, strengthen Customs border enforcement and search powers, modernise customs procedures, define tobacco content for duty, and amend the Export Market Development Grants scheme. Key changes include removing the air liability cap with claims up to 100,000 SDR (about A$172,000), and raising the EMDG maximum grant to $200,000, the turnover limit to $50 million, and lowering the expenditure threshold to $10,000.

speeches.speaker: Dana Wortley
speeches.brief: The report of the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Public Administration on the Families, Housing, Community Services and Indigenous Affairs and Other Legislation Amendment (2008 Budget and Other Measures) Bill 2008 was presented, with the order that it be printed.

speeches.speaker: Cory Bernardi
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the $55 billion in family support would not have been possible without the former Howard government's economic management, and criticised the Labor government for imposing means tests on the baby bonus and Family Tax Benefit Part B at a $150,000 income threshold, affecting 40,000 families, as well as changes to the Commonwealth seniors health card affecting 27,000 seniors and the partner service pension affecting 930 veterans' partners.

speeches.speaker: Ursula Stephens
speeches.brief: Senator Bernardi moved opposition amendments requiring an independent review of the bill’s operation by June 2010 and opposing schedules that would change the seniors health card and partner service pension, arguing the government had not disclosed these cuts before the election and that they would harm 930 veteran partners and thousands of seniors.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Murray
speeches.brief: Senator Siewert moved amendments to raise the fringe benefits tax cap for not-for-profit organisations from $30,000 to $40,000 and introduce ongoing indexation, citing a sector workforce crisis and estimating a cost of $80–100 million against the sector's $50 billion value. The government opposed the amendments as piecemeal, citing Treasury costings of $740–805 million, and the opposition cited a lack of agreed financial modelling; both amendments were negatived.

The House agreed to Senate amendments 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 to the Families, Housing, Community Services and Indigenous Affairs and Other Legislation Amendment (2008 Budget and Other Measures) Bill 2008, but disagreed to amendments 4 and 5, and the Senate ordered immediate consideration in Committee of the Whole.

speeches.speaker: Joe Ludwig
speeches.brief: The opposition will not insist on amendments 4 and 5 to avoid delaying the bill, but argues the government is stripping $20 million in entitlements from 930 seniors and veterans while spending $167 million on pork-barrelling in marginal electorates.
